what: Using RainAttr for Attribution and SATE Analysis: Oman Data Example
title: Introduction to RainAttr
text: package estimates performs inference attribution, defined percentage increase raw-scale rainfall attributable ionization technology, sample average treatment effect (SATE) gauge-day level rainfall enhancement trial data. example gauge-day level dataset given : Gauge.Day.Type column classifies observation one following types: Upwind: gauges located upwind ionizers Target: gauges located downwind least one active ionizers Control: gauges located downwind inactive ionizers Scope: gauges neither upwind, target, control

previous_headings: Using RainAttr for Attribution and SATE Analysis: Oman Data Example
title: Introduction to RainAttr
text: examine effectiveness ionization technology used Oman 2013-2018 trial, based two-stage linear mixed model (LMM) approach employed Chambers, Beare, et al. (2022). achieved using main function rain_attr package: rain_attr function fits two LMMs sequentially: Obtain fitted values (named instr_pred_name) data[downwind_subset & positive_subset,], fitted values conditional unconditional depending `instr_pred_type’. downwind (second-stage) LMM fitted using lme4::lmer(downwind_lmm_formula) data[downwind_subset & positive_subset,]. estimated LMM model parameters used calculate attribution SATE estimates, attr_type specifies type correction back-transformation bias computing attribution estimates, x_downwind_name identifies non-ionizer related covariates, whose effects excluded calculation estimates. Moreover, logistic propensity score model also fitted using glm(downwind_propensity_formula, family = "binomial") data[downwind_subset & positive_subset,] response binary indicator whether observation exposed ionizer (.e., target observation). fitted model, along arguments specified via downwind_target_subset downwind_control_subset, facilitate estimation SATEs. different options can specified via arguments rain_attr(), example illustrates recommended options: instr_pred_type = 'Conditional': uses conditional fitted values upwind (first-stage) LMM downwind_lmm_formula = LogRain - natural_pred ~ ...: incorporates conditional fitted values offset term attr_type = 'ThoEtAl': attribution estimation based adjustment proposed Tho et al. (2026) account back-transformation bias arising modelling log-transformed rainfall target_only = FALSE (default option, hence explicitly specified ): attribution estimates computed using treated (exposed operating ionizers) control (exposed) observations.
code: result = rain_attr(   #gauge-day level trial data   data = oman,    #LMM formula fitted to the upwind (first-stage) observations   upwind_lmm_formula = LogRain ~  Gauge.Elevation + Steering.Wind.Speed + Total.Totals + PC2.Dry.Temperature + PC1.Relative.Humidity + PC1.Ground.Level.Pressure + (1|TrialDay),    #Variable name for storing instrumental prediction from upwind (first-stage) LMM   instr_pred_name = 'natural_pred',    #Types of instrumental prediction: 'Unconditional' or 'Conditional'   instr_pred_type = 'Conditional',    #LMM formula fitted to the downwind (second-stage) observations   downwind_lmm_formula = LogRain - natural_pred ~ Gauge.Elevation  + Target.H.01 + Target.H.02 + Target.H.03 + Target.H.04 + Target.H.05 + Target.H.06 + Target.H.07 + Target.H.08 + Target.H.09 + Target.H.10 + Gauge.Elevation:Target.H.01 + Gauge.Elevation:Target.H.02 + (1|TrialDay),    #Formula for fitting a logistic regression model to the indicator of rainfall event (used for bootstrapping of rainfall events)   downwind_logistic_formula = NULL,    #Formula for fitting the propensity score model to downwind observations, where responses are indicators of whether each downwind observations is a 'Target'   downwind_propensity_formula = (Gauge.Day.Type == 'Target') ~ Total.Totals + PC1.Dry.Temperature + PC1.Relative.Humidity + PC1.Ground.Level.Pressure,    #Specify the column in input data that contains the raw rainfall   rain_col_name = 'Rain.Gauge.Measurement',    #Logical expression identifying subset of observations to which upwind_lmm_formula is fitted   upwind_subset = Gauge.Day.Type == 'Upwind',    #Logical expression identifying subset of observations to which downwind_lmm_formula is fitted   downwind_subset = Gauge.Day.Type  %in% c('Target','Control'),    #Logical expression identifying subset of observations of those that are 'Target'   downwind_target_subset = Gauge.Day.Type == 'Target',    #Logical expression identifying subset of observations of those that are 'Control'   downwind_control_subset = Gauge.Day.Type == 'Control',    #Logical expression identifying subset of observations with rainfall event   positive_subset = Rain.Gauge.Measurement > 0,      #Types of correction (for back-transformation bias) used for computing the attribution estimate: 'ChambersEtAl', 'ChambersEtAl_No_Winsorize', 'ThoEtAl', or 'No'   attr_type = 'ThoEtAl',    #Vector of variable names in downwind_lmm_formula to identify non-ionizer related covariates, whose effects are not included in the calculation of attribution and SATE   x_downwind_name = c('Gauge.Elevation')   )

Fit downwind (second stage) LMM using  lme4::lmer(downwind_lmm_formula) subset observations data satisfying downwind_subset & positive_subset. $$y_{ij} =  x_{ij}^\top \alpha + z_{ij}^\top \beta + u_i + e_{ij}  $$ \(\) indexes day (group) \(j\) indexes gauge (unit within group), \(x_{ij}\) vector covariates (names supplied x_downwind_name, including intercept) related ionizers (treatment), \(z_{ij}\) vector ionizer (treatment) related covariates, \(u_i\) random intercepts, \(e_{ij}\) error terms. fitted values obtained upwind (first stage) LMM can either : Included covariate right-hand side downwind_lmm_formula, e.g., instr_pred_name = "natural_pred" downwind_lmm_formula = LogRain ~ natural_pred + ..., Included offset term subtracting response left-hand side, e.g., instr_pred_name = "natural_pred" downwind_lmm_formula = LogRain - natural_pred ~ .... Attribution  Two attribution estimates, namely apo apl computed based estimated fixed effect coefficients \(\hat{\alpha}\), \(\hat{\beta}\) EBLUPs \(\hat{u}_i\) fitted downwind (second stage) LMM. apo represents total increase decrease downwind rainfall attributed ionizer (treatment) proportion total amount observed downwind rainfall., apl represents total increase decrease downwind rainfall attributed ionizer (treatment) proportion total expected amount downwind rainfall without effect ionizer (treatment). function allows three different ways estimating apo apl specified argument attr_type: ChambersEtAl Attribution estimated based approach Chambers et al. (2022a), adjust back-transformation bias due modelling log-transformed rainfall: $$     \code{apo} = \sum_{(,j)} Rain_{ij} [ 1 - \max\{\lambda^{-1} \exp(-z_{ij}^\top \hat{\beta}), 0.5\} ] /  \sum_{(,j)}Rain_{ij}, \quad     \code{apl} = \sum_{(,j)} Rain_{ij} [ 1 -
